title: Bounded cleaning stages
statement: Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $k$ Boolean work tapes, let $q_1$ be a state, and fix an input, input-head position, tape contents $D_t,M_t$, head positions $D_p$, output word, and integer $B\ge 0$. Assume that for each tape $j$ there are integers $a,b$ with $a\le0\le b$, $-B\le a-1$, $b+1\le B$, $a\le D_p(j)\le b$, and such that changing the marked-tape contents at $D_p(j)$ according to the prescribed write rule produces the tape that marks the origin and every cell from $a$ through $b$; also assume every nonblank cell of $D_t(j)$ lies between $a$ and $b$. Then, for every $n,i\in\mathbb N$ with $i+n=k$, there is a finite time $T$ such that throughout the cleaning-machine run from stage $i$, all work-tape head positions have absolute value at most $B$, and at time $T$ the configuration is stage $k$ with the same input-head position, tape data, head positions, and output.
